native.notes: Covers parsing, redirects and DNS. The OWASP excerpt only says DNS resolution can bind a legit domain to an internal IP. It does not contain the TOCTOU, connect-to-validated-IP or SNI details, the backslash parser example, or 'avoid full URLs' advice. The deny-list claim (#7) was not scored because of the 8-claim cap; PortSwigger supports it. Limits are honestly disclosed, including that the Wikipedia link to SSRF is an inference. No challenging evidence.

sibyl.notes: The quoted OWASP sentence is not in the excerpt. Only the general DNS-binding risk appears, so the claim is partial. The OWASP resolve-once/SNI/retries fix claim was not scored (cap) and is also absent from the excerpt. The behradtaher claims (egress proxy, IMDSv2 limits, resolver caching caveat) were not scored but are supported. The caveats narrow the claim, but the answer admits no counterevidence search.

deep_research.notes: Thorough coverage. The OWASP excerpt lacks the TOCTOU, connect-to-validated-IP, SNI and retries content. The blocklist and defense-in-depth/IMDSv2 claims were not scored (cap); PortSwigger supports the encodings, and IMDSv2 is not in the OWASP excerpt. The DNS pinning limitations and the disclosed gaps (no prevalence data, Wikipedia covers browsers only) count as attempted counterevidence. The method note about tooling is irrelevant to the question.
